# The Crown That Circles the North

## Scripture
"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name. Great is our Lord and mighty in power; his understanding has no limit." — Psalm 147:4-5

## Reflection
Step outside on an October evening and face north. If the skies are dark enough, you may find the constellation Corona Borealis—the Northern Crown—a delicate semicircle of stars arcing above the horizon. It isn't the brightest or largest constellation, yet it holds a quiet dignity, a circlet of light worn by the sky itself.

Scripture tells us God determines the number of the stars and calls each by name. Not one is overlooked. Not one wanders unnamed through the dark. The same God who set that crown in place, star by star, knows you with the same intimate attention. He does not merely count you among the multitudes—He calls you by name.

In a season when the world grows loud and hurried, the Northern Crown reminds us that God's care is not scattered or distracted. His understanding has no limit. The One who named every star also knows your worries, your waiting, your quiet hopes. You are not lost in the vastness. You are held within it.

Tonight, let the crown of stars be a small sign of a greater truth: the King of all creation knows His own, and He has not forgotten you.

## Prayer
Lord of the stars, You call each one by name—and You call me Your own. When I feel small beneath the vastness of the night, remind me that Your understanding has no limit and Your love has no end. Hold me close as I rest beneath the crown of Your creation. Amen.
